project.name: Exasol Studio
project.description: Whole-repo graph. Tauri 2 (Rust) + React 19 desktop Exasol client with a Node agent-core AI sidecar, ANTLR SQL parser, database-side semantic-views layer, vendored AI agent skills, CI/CD, docs, and knowledge tooling.

nodes.name: _build-package.yml
nodes.summary: Reusable GitHub Actions workflow that packages every Marketplace item: a cheap change-check compares the upstream latest tag against the last mirrored version, and only when it changed does it build a Python wheel (kind=wheel) or mirror upstream release assets (kind=mirror) to a mirror-<id> release.
nodes.languageNotes: workflow_call reusable workflow with typed inputs (id/repo/kind/package); change-gating avoids paying build cost on weeks with no upstream release.

nodes.name: exasol-sql-parser.yml
nodes.summary: Path-filtered CI workflow that tests the ANTLR-based exasol-sql-parser package on pushes and PRs, running the pnpm generate, typecheck, and test steps under a Java 17 + Node 22 toolchain.

nodes.name: pkg-agent-skills.yml
nodes.summary: Thin scheduled caller workflow that mirrors the exasol-labs/exasol-agent-skills release assets into the marketplace by delegating to the reusable _build-package workflow (kind=mirror).

nodes.name: pkg-ai-lab.yml
nodes.summary: Thin scheduled caller workflow that mirrors the exasol/ai-lab release assets into the marketplace via the reusable _build-package workflow (kind=mirror).

nodes.name: pkg-exapump.yml
nodes.summary: Thin scheduled caller workflow that mirrors the exasol-labs/exapump release assets into the marketplace via the reusable _build-package workflow (kind=mirror).

nodes.name: pkg-json-tables.yml
nodes.summary: Commit-gated marketplace build workflow for exasol-json-tables that cross-compiles the Rust json_to_parquet ingest engine across Linux/macOS/Windows and builds a Python wheel, then publishes the prebuilt binaries plus wheel to the mirror-json-tables release so end users need no Rust toolchain.
nodes.languageNotes: check/ingest(matrix)/wheel/publish job DAG with a cross-platform build matrix and artifact upload/download fan-in.

nodes.name: pkg-mcp-server.yml
nodes.summary: Thin scheduled caller workflow that builds a Python wheel of the exasol-mcp-server package (exasol/mcp-server) via the reusable _build-package workflow (kind=wheel).

nodes.name: pkg-pyexasol.yml
nodes.summary: Thin scheduled caller workflow that builds a Python wheel of the pyexasol package (exasol/pyexasol) via the reusable _build-package workflow (kind=wheel).

nodes.name: refresh-runtime-components.yml
nodes.summary: Daily automation workflow that resolves the latest compatible immutable set of bundled runtime components (Nano image, python-stack, semantic-views, agent skills), validates the candidate by building the app and running an MCP/semantic-views integration smoke test across five platforms, then opens an automated PR when anything changed.
nodes.languageNotes: refresh/validate(matrix)/commit job DAG with SHA-pinned actions, a git patch artifact passed between jobs, and embedded Python driving a Docker-hosted Exasol Nano MCP handshake.

nodes.name: release-app.yml
nodes.summary: Tag-triggered release workflow that builds every Exasol Studio distribution (macOS Apple Silicon/Intel, Windows x64, Linux x64/arm64) via tauri-action, bundles the platform runtime and Exasol components, then renames assets to friendly names and publishes the Homebrew cask + Scoop manifest.
nodes.languageNotes: A plan job emits a dispatch-filterable build matrix so a single failed distribution can be rebuilt without paying for all six runners.

nodes.name: update-catalog.yml
nodes.summary: Scheduled workflow that regenerates marketplace/catalog.json — the app's single source of truth for each item's latest upstream version and mirror tag — by querying the GitHub releases API, committing only when the catalog actually changed.

nodes.name: verify-runtime-components.yml
nodes.summary: Path-filtered pull-request check that verifies the provenance of the bundled runtime components by re-running the refresh script in --verify mode against the committed lock, python-stack, semantic-views, and agent skills.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index for the semantic-views SQL example set, listing each example file, the required run order (physical model before model seed), and the Python tooling used to generate the OSI and Databricks interoperability exports.

nodes.name: sales_databricks_metric_view.yaml
nodes.summary: Databricks Unity Catalog Metric View definition over the MART sales tables, declaring the source, joins, dimension fields, and measures; used as an import example to translate a Databricks metric view into an Exasol semantic model.
nodes.languageNotes: Databricks Unity Catalog metric-view schema (source/joins/fields/measures) rather than an Exasol-native format.

nodes.name: sales_materializations.sql
nodes.summary: Builds an aggregate materialization table for revenue-by-region and registers it with the semantic model via SEMANTIC_ADMIN.REGISTER_MATERIALIZATION plus dimension/metric column mappings.

nodes.name: sales_metrics_semantic_definition.sql
nodes.summary: Semantic-SQL metric authoring example that uses ALTER SEMANTIC VIEW to declare facts (net revenue/cost, quantity) and metrics (total revenue, gross margin, completed revenue) on the sales model, illustrating the target Semantic SQL surface.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses proposed Exasol Semantic SQL DDL (SEMANTIC VIEW / FACT / METRIC clauses) not standard SQL.

nodes.name: sales_model_fixup.sql
nodes.summary: One-time corrective script for a live sales model that rewrites the order_quarter dimension expression to a valid Exasol function, deletes a leftover test dimension, and revalidates the model.

nodes.name: sales_model_seed.sql
nodes.summary: Seeds the full sales semantic model by invoking SEMANTIC_ADMIN scripts to create the model and register its entities (order_line, order, customer, product) with grains, joins, dimensions, and metrics over the MART tables.
nodes.languageNotes: Model is defined procedurally through EXECUTE SCRIPT SEMANTIC_ADMIN.* Lua/UDF calls rather than declarative DDL.

nodes.name: sales_osi.yaml
nodes.summary: Apache Ossie / OSI 0.2.0.dev0 interoperability export of the sales semantic model, serving as an import/export interchange example (not an install script) generated by tools/osi.py.
nodes.languageNotes: OSI (Open Semantic Interchange) YAML format for cross-tool semantic model portability.

nodes.name: sales_physical_model.sql
nodes.summary: Creates and populates the physical MART schema with CUSTOMERS, PRODUCTS, ORDERS, and ORDER_LINES tables plus seed rows, providing the base data the sales semantic model is built on. Must run before the model seed.

nodes.name: sales_semantic_queries.sql
nodes.summary: Example introspection queries against the SEMANTIC_CATALOG views (MODELS, OBJECT_COLUMNS, METRICS) to inspect the registered sales model, its columns, and its metrics.

nodes.name: MART.CUSTOMERS
nodes.summary: Customer dimension table keyed by CUSTOMER_ID with name and region attributes.

nodes.name: MART.PRODUCTS
nodes.summary: Product dimension table keyed by PRODUCT_ID with name and category attributes.

nodes.name: MART.ORDERS
nodes.summary: Order header fact table keyed by ORDER_ID with customer reference, order date, and status.

nodes.name: MART.ORDER_LINES
nodes.summary: Order-line grain fact table with composite key (ORDER_ID, LINE_ID) capturing quantity, net unit price, and unit cost — the base grain for revenue and margin metrics.

nodes.name: MART.SALES_REVENUE_BY_REGION
nodes.summary: Aggregate materialization table of total revenue grouped by customer region, joined across order lines, orders, and customers.

nodes.name: 000_create_schemas.sql
nodes.summary: First install step that creates the four Exasol Semantic Views schemas (SYS_SEMANTIC internal catalog, SEMANTIC_CATALOG readable views, SEMANTIC_ADMIN Lua scripts, SEMANTIC_AGENT discovery views) plus the discovery marker tables.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS and COMMENT ON SCHEMA for idempotent installs.

nodes.name: 001_create_semantic_catalog.sql
nodes.summary: Defines the 34 internal catalog tables in SYS_SEMANTIC that store the semantic model: models, versions, entities, relationships, dimensions, facts, metrics, validation runs, materializations, and agent request logs.
nodes.languageNotes: Exasol DDL using DECIMAL(18,0) IDENTITY primary keys and large VARCHAR(2000000) description columns.

nodes.name: 002_create_semantic_catalog_views.sql
nodes.summary: Creates 30 readable SEMANTIC_CATALOG views over the SYS_SEMANTIC tables, exposing models, metrics, lineage, compatible dimensions, and current validation issues for consumers.
nodes.languageNotes: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW joins across the internal catalog tables to present user-facing projections.

nodes.name: 003_create_semantic_admin_scripts.sql
nodes.summary: Generated 11k-line bundle installing the SEMANTIC_ADMIN Lua runtime scripts (admin, compiler, validation, publish, preprocessor, agent) packaged from lua/semantic_layer/; must not be edited by hand.
nodes.languageNotes: Auto-generated by package_lua_scripts.py; edit the Lua sources and re-run the installer instead of this file.

nodes.name: 004_create_semantic_preprocessor.sql
nodes.summary: Registers the SEMANTIC_ADMIN.SEMANTIC_PREPROCESSOR Lua SQL preprocessor that rewrites semantic queries via the definition runtime and compiler before execution.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Exasol CREATE OR REPLACE LUA PREPROCESSOR SCRIPT and exa.import to wire in the compiler and definition runtimes.

nodes.name: 005_create_semantic_surface_helpers.sql
nodes.summary: Creates SEMANTIC_ADMIN surface helper scripts including SEMANTIC_GUARD, PUBLISH_MODEL, REFRESH_SEMANTIC_SURFACE, and the ENABLE/DISABLE_SEMANTIC_SQL session toggles for the preprocessor.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixes Lua scalar scripts with EXECUTE-style admin scripts separated by the '/' statement delimiter.

nodes.name: 006_create_semantic_agent_views.sql
nodes.summary: Creates 11 agent-scoped SEMANTIC_AGENT discovery views (models, objects, fields, valid combinations, measure groups, glossary, verified queries, request history) that expose the semantic catalog to AI agents.
nodes.languageNotes: Views suffixed _FOR_AGENT flatten catalog metadata into agent-consumable projections.

nodes.name: METRICS

nodes.name: MATERIALIZATIONS
nodes.summary: SYS_SEMANTIC.MATERIALIZATIONS table tracking materialized surfaces of semantic objects along with their column mappings.

nodes.name: VERIFIED_QUERIES
nodes.summary: SYS_SEMANTIC.VERIFIED_QUERIES table storing curated, trusted example queries surfaced to agents as few-shot guidance.

nodes.name: AGENT_REQUEST_LOG
nodes.summary: SYS_SEMANTIC.AGENT_REQUEST_LOG table logging agent semantic-query requests for history, feedback, and suggestion generation.

nodes.name: MODELS_FOR_AGENT
nodes.summary: SEMANTIC_AGENT.MODELS_FOR_AGENT view presenting published models with version and preprocessor context for agent discovery.

nodes.name: FIELDS_FOR_AGENT
nodes.summary: SEMANTIC_AGENT.FIELDS_FOR_AGENT view flattening dimensions, facts, and metrics into a single agent-consumable field listing per model.

nodes.name: VALID_COMBINATIONS_FOR_AGENT
nodes.summary: SEMANTIC_AGENT.VALID_COMBINATIONS_FOR_AGENT view enumerating which metric and dimension combinations are queryable together, guiding agents away from invalid joins.

nodes.name: BUSINESS_GLOSSARY_FOR_AGENT
nodes.summary: SEMANTIC_AGENT.BUSINESS_GLOSSARY_FOR_AGENT view exposing synonyms and descriptions as a business glossary so agents can map natural-language terms to catalog objects.

nodes.summary: Extracts ColumnMeta (name plus type name) for every column of a result row.

nodes.name: fetch_all_rows
nodes.summary: Runs a SQL statement on the pool and collects every row as JSON — the shared helper used by connection and metadata probes.

nodes.name: split_statements
nodes.summary: Splits a multi-statement SQL script into individual statements, respecting string literals, quoted identifiers and comments so semicolons inside them are not treated as separators.

nodes.name: parse_activity_percent
nodes.summary: Parses the progress percentage out of an Exasol session activity string; hoisted to a top-level function so it can be unit tested directly.

nodes.name: is_result_set_statement
nodes.summary: Classifies a statement as result-set producing or row-count producing so the executor knows which path to take.

nodes.name: describe_columns
nodes.summary: Describes a statement's output columns without fetching rows, used to return metadata for empty result sets.

nodes.name: run_statement
nodes.summary: Executes a single statement against the pool, streaming rows up to the row cap, tracking truncation, and recording execution and fetch timings separately.

nodes.name: execute_sql
nodes.summary: Tauri command that executes a SQL script end to end: resolves the pool, optionally splits statements, runs each one, emits progress events, and appends the run to SQL history.

nodes.name: csv-import.test.ts
nodes.summary: Zero-dependency node:test suite covering the agent-core CSV/Parquet ingestion pipeline end to end: delimiter sniffing, quoted-field and BOM handling, header synthesis, Exasol identifier case-folding and dedupe, type inference with precision/scale sizing, SQL literal rendering, and DDL/INSERT construction. Treats the module's failure modes as data corruption and SQL injection rather than cosmetic bugs, so it asserts quote escaping, NULL fallbacks for values that do not fit their inferred type, NULL padding of short rows, and regression guards against head-only sampling and stack overflow on very large columns.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the built-in node:test runner with describe/test and node:assert/strict — no external test framework — and imports the module under test with an explicit .ts extension (native TypeScript execution).

nodes.name: loop.ts
nodes.summary: The heart of the agent-core sidecar: orchestrates a single conversational turn as a LangGraph state machine (attempt → recover → continuation → finalize), wiring provider selection, skill injection, knowledge-base retrieval, tool selection, streaming session events, and memory extraction. Also exports the text heuristics that detect when a model narrated work instead of calling tools.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a LangGraph turn graph with named node functions closed over the turn's local state, so the whole 760-line runTurn body doubles as the graph's dependency-injection scope.

nodes.name: runTurn
nodes.summary: Executes one full agent turn: resolves the provider/model, ingests attachments, assembles the system prompt from skills, memory and knowledge-base context, selects and wraps tools, then drives the LangGraph turn graph and persists results plus extracted memories.

nodes.name: humanizeProviderError
nodes.summary: Maps raw provider error strings (invalid key, quota, rate limit, context overflow, network, overload) onto short user-facing explanations, falling back to a truncated raw message.

nodes.name: buildRetrievedContext
nodes.summary: Builds the grounding block injected into the system prompt by querying the knowledge graph for a schema overview, matching table cards, join hubs and subsystems for the user's question.

nodes.name: selectTools
nodes.summary: Narrows the full tool set down to those plausibly needed for the turn by keyword-matching the user text, keeping a core baseline plus any MCP-prefixed tools.

nodes.name: wrapForProgress
nodes.summary: Decorates every tool's execute function so repeated identical calls are counted and short-circuited, guarding the loop against models that hammer the same tool with the same arguments.

nodes.name: looksLikeUnacted
nodes.summary: Heuristic that detects assistant text describing work it never performed — leaked tool-call markup, raw SQL blocks, or planning phrases like "I'll run…" — so the loop can force a real tool call.

nodes.name: extractReadSql
nodes.summary: Pulls a single read-only SELECT/WITH statement out of assistant prose or a fenced code block, rejecting anything containing write or DDL keywords so the rescue path can only replay safe queries.

nodes.name: looksUnfinished
nodes.summary: Detects a reply that trails off mid-plan ("I'll now check…", "moving on to…") so the turn graph can issue a continuation prompt; matches both ASCII and typographic apostrophes.
nodes.languageNotes: The apostrophe class ['’] matters because model output routinely uses U+2019 rather than ASCII "'".

nodes.name: summarize
nodes.summary: Condenses an arbitrary tool result into a one-line progress string for session events, preferring a report's first line or a row count.

nodes.name: server.ts
nodes.summary: HTTP sidecar entry point: starts a token-authenticated Node http server exposing the agent-core REST/SSE surface (providers, settings, connections, sessions, SQL generation, audit, MCP, dashboards, skills, artifacts). Recently shrank from 808 to 574 lines after four verbatim duplicates of one route block were removed, leaving occurrences 2-4 unreachable dead code.
nodes.languageNotes: All routing lives in one long createServer handler using manual URL path-segment matching rather than a framework router — which is why duplicated route blocks silently became unreachable.

nodes.name: startServer
nodes.summary: Boots the sidecar: mints a bearer token, connects MCP servers, and registers every HTTP route — provider probing and credential storage, settings updates, connection registration with knowledge-base refresh, SQL generation, and the session/agent-turn endpoints.

nodes.name: loop.heuristics.test.ts
nodes.summary: Zero-dependency node:test suite covering the three text heuristics exported by loop.ts — looksLikeUnacted, extractReadSql and looksUnfinished — including the typographic-apostrophe and write-statement-rejection edge cases.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs on the built-in node:test runner with node:assert/strict and a direct ./loop.ts specifier, so it needs no test framework dependency.

nodes.name: tool-repair.test.ts
nodes.summary: Zero-dependency node:test suite exercising the whole tool-repair surface — resolveToolName, parseLooseArgs, repairArgs, extractTextToolCalls, zodSchemaish, repairCall and rescueTextCalls — with malformed-JSON, alias and phantom-tool edge cases.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Short, standard-named cross-tool agent instruction file (Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Claude Code) that points at CLAUDE.md as the authoritative version and restates the non-negotiable always-rules: consult the committed knowledge graphs first, refresh them after every change, get a Codex review, and obey the three KISS hard rules. Also documents the zero-dependency test setup (`pnpm test`, `pnpm test:coverage`, Node `node:test` + Rust `#[cfg(test)]`, no vitest/jest).
nodes.languageNotes: AGENTS.md is an emerging cross-vendor convention: a tool-agnostic filename that many AI coding assistants auto-load, here deliberately kept as a thin pointer so CLAUDE.md stays the single source of truth.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Authoritative agent and contributor guide for the repo, covering the three knowledge tools (understand-anything graph, graphify, llm-wiki/obsidian-vault), the mandatory code-quality workflow (Codex review, KISS + SOLID, edge-case unit tests), the three KISS hard rules on file size, unreachable code and testability, how to run the test suites, and the conventions that bite (icons over emoji, theme-safe CSS, single cross-platform frontend, local build, commit rules).
nodes.languageNotes: Documents a deliberate no-test-framework decision: Node's built-in `node:test` plus Rust `#[cfg(test)]`, keeping the toolchain dependency-free — contributors are explicitly told not to add vitest or jest.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Private root workspace manifest (pnpm 11.7.0) that defines repo-wide tooling scripts rather than shipping code: desktop dev/build/typecheck delegates into apps/desktop, the `test` script fans out to agent-core, exasol-sql-parser and Rust cargo tests, `test:coverage` reports on the logic core, and the graphify scripts run the knowledge-graph check/render/HTML pipeline.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `pnpm --dir <pkg> <script>` delegation and `"$npm_node_execpath"` instead of a bare `node`, so the graphify tooling always runs under the same Node binary pnpm itself was invoked with.

nodes.name: knowledge-tools.md
nodes.summary: Setup and usage guide for the project's four knowledge systems — graphify (AST codebase graph), llm-wiki (durable decisions KB), obsidian-vault (design notes) and the committed understand-anything `.ua/` graph — covering one-time installation, the read/write working loop, and which artifacts are committed versus git-ignored.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown reference doc organised around a capability table plus copy-pasteable shell setup blocks; it also encodes repo policy (which generated artifacts are committed and why `docs/codebase-graph.html` is a frozen snapshot).

nodes.name: kiss-hard-rules.md
nodes.summary: llm-wiki page recording three mandatory KISS rules — cap file size (split at ~500 lines), never ship unreachable code, and keep logic small enough to unit-test — backed by the `server.ts` 234-line dead-code precedent, the deliberate no-test-framework decision (`node:test` + Rust `#[cfg(test)]`), and the two real defects the first test pass surfaced.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown wiki page with YAML frontmatter (title/category/status) following the llm-wiki convention; it names offending source files and line counts directly, so it functions as an actionable refactor backlog rather than abstract guidance.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Package manifest for the private `@exasol-studio/agent-core` sidecar: declares the ESM entry point and `exa-agent` binary, esbuild bundling scripts for the server / CLI / MCP gateway, LangChain + MCP SDK runtime dependencies, and dependency-free `test` / `test:watch` / `test:coverage` scripts built on Node's `node:test`.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Node's built-in `node:test` runner rather than vitest/jest, so the test scripts add zero dependencies; coverage is deliberately scoped with `--test-coverage-include` to the pure logic core (`tool-repair.ts`, `csv-import.ts`) instead of the whole package.

tour.title: What Is Exasol Studio
tour.description: Start here to understand the product's purpose and shape. The README frames Exasol Studio as a desktop client for Exasol databases with an in-app AI assistant, while the knowledge-vault overview note gives the one-page architecture picture: a Tauri 2 + React 19 shell, a Rust orchestration core, and a Node agent-core sidecar. Read these two first so every later step has a place to hang.

tour.title: Architecture & Contributor Map
tour.description: Before touching code, absorb the mental model the maintainers use. CLAUDE.md is the contributor/agent guide describing the Tauri 2 + React 19 stack, the workspace layout, and conventions; the foundation architecture doc lays out the layered boundaries and design patterns. Together they explain WHY the system is split into a frontend, a Rust backend, and a separate AI sidecar — the three runtime pieces the rest of the tour walks through.

tour.title: The Decisions That Shaped It
tour.description: The Architecture Decision Records capture the load-bearing choices. ADR-0002 explains why Tauri v2 + Rust was chosen as the desktop host over Electron, and ADR-0004 defines AI as a 'governed action layer' with explicit context disclosure and redaction — the rule that constrains how the agent-core sidecar in Step 9 is allowed to act. Reading these now means later design details will feel intentional rather than arbitrary.

tour.title: React Frontend Boot
tour.description: Now follow the runtime from the user's screen inward. main.tsx is the React entry point that mounts the root component into the DOM inside the Tauri webview, and App.tsx is the root component that wires providers and renders the application shell and layout. This is the 'front door' of everything the user sees.
tour.languageLesson: React 19 apps bootstrap through createRoot(...).render(<App/>). Provider components wrap the tree to inject shared context (theme, connection state, query client) so descendants can consume it via hooks instead of prop-drilling.

tour.title: The Studio Shell
tour.description: ExasolStudio.tsx is the roughly 5,000-line application shell that App.tsx renders: it wires together the title bar, the connection panel, the SQL editor, results grids, and the Exa assistant into one cohesive workspace. Building on the boot sequence from Step 4, this is where the UI's feature modules meet — and the highest fan-out React file in the project, making it the best single map of the frontend.

tour.title: Crossing Into Rust: The Tauri Backend
tour.description: When the React UI needs to touch the database, filesystem, or OS, it calls across the Tauri bridge into Rust. main.rs is a thin binary that delegates to the library crate's run function, and lib.rs is the real entry point: it declares every backend module and registers the command handlers the frontend invokes. lib.rs has the highest fan-out in the whole repo, so it doubles as the table of contents for the backend.
tour.languageLesson: Tauri v2 exposes Rust functions to JavaScript via #[tauri::command] and the invoke_handler registered in lib.rs. main.rs stays thin so the crate can also be compiled as a library for tests; the tauri::Builder assembles plugins, state, and command handlers before .run() starts the event loop.

tour.title: SQL Execution, Connections & the Vault
tour.description: These are the core backend command modules that make Studio a database client. query.rs is the SQL execution engine that splits multi-statement scripts and runs them against a pooled Exasol connection; local_database.rs bootstraps a local Exasol Personal instance; and security.rs is the encryption vault that seals connection secrets with AEAD behind a master password. This trio is the beating heart of the runtime path that began at the SQL editor in Step 5.

tour.title: Local Runtime, Local LLM & Marketplace
tour.description: Studio can run entirely on the user's machine, and these modules make that possible. local_runtime.rs manages the local Exasol runtime lifecycle (Personal launcher and containerized nano); local_llm.rs installs and runs a bundled local LLM so the assistant works offline; and market.rs installs ecosystem tooling (uv, ai-lab, Personal) through the in-app Marketplace. Together they explain how the app provisions its own dependencies rather than assuming a pre-set-up environment.

tour.title: Exa: The Agent-Core Sidecar
tour.description: Exa, the in-app assistant, lives in a separate Node process called agent-core. index.ts bootstraps that process and dispatches into the server or CLI; server.ts is a dependency-free localhost HTTP + SSE server that the desktop app talks to; and loop.ts is the agent turn orchestrator that assembles context, selects tools, runs the model loop, and streams results. This is the concrete implementation of the governed AI action model from ADR-0004 in Step 3.
tour.languageLesson: The agent loop is the classic reason/act cycle: build a prompt from context, call the model, parse any tool calls, execute them, feed results back, and repeat until the model stops. Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream partial tokens to the UI over a single long-lived HTTP response instead of polling.

tour.title: The Exasol SQL Parser
tour.description: Smart editing (autocomplete, validation) is powered by a standalone ANTLR grammar package. index.ts re-exports the getSuggestions completion API; completion.ts computes caret-position suggestions using antlr4-c3 against the real grammar; and ExasolParser.ts is the generated parser itself — one of the most depended-upon files in the repo. This package is what lets the SQL editor from Step 5 understand Exasol dialect rather than just highlight keywords.
tour.languageLesson: ANTLR generates a lexer + parser from a .g4 grammar; the generated files are committed but never hand-edited. antlr4-c3 walks the parser's ATN (augmented transition network) from the caret token to compute exactly which token kinds are grammatically valid next — that's how context-aware completion is derived from the grammar itself.

tour.title: The Semantic Views SQL Layer
tour.description: Studio ships a database-side SQL layer that installs a semantic catalog into Exasol. The install README documents the ordered sequence of SQL files; 000_create_schemas.sql creates the four schemas (including the SYS_SEMANTIC internal catalog); and 001_create_semantic_catalog.sql defines the 34 catalog tables that store the semantic model. This is the server-side counterpart to the client — the data model the assistant and BI features reason over.
tour.languageLesson: Numbered SQL install scripts (000, 001, 002...) are a lightweight migration pattern: each file is applied in order and should be idempotent so re-running the install is safe. Separating schemas (000) from catalog tables (001) keeps the namespace setup independent of the objects placed inside it.

tour.title: Vendored Agent Skills
tour.description: The assistant's domain knowledge is packaged as vendored 'skills' — Markdown playbooks loaded into the agent's context. exasol-sql.md covers dialect essentials like LIMIT/QUALIFY and uppercase identifier folding, and the exasol-database grammar reference gives statement-level coverage across DQL/DML/DDL. These are how Exa (Step 9) is taught Exasol-specific behavior without retraining a model — knowledge as versioned files, mirrored from upstream by CI.

tour.title: CI/CD: Building & Shipping
tour.description: Now step back to how the whole system is built and delivered. release-app.yml is the tag-triggered workflow that builds every Studio distribution (macOS Apple Silicon/Intel, Windows, Linux), while _build-package.yml is the reusable workflow every Marketplace item calls — it change-gates on the upstream tag so build cost is only paid when something actually changed. This ties together the Marketplace tooling from Step 8 and the vendored skills from Step 12.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions reusable workflows (workflow_call) accept typed inputs and are invoked by other workflows like functions, avoiding copy-pasted YAML. Change-gating — comparing an upstream latest tag against the last mirrored version before building — keeps scheduled pipelines cheap on weeks with no new release.

tour.title: Knowledge Bases & Repo Tooling
tour.description: Finish with the cross-cutting knowledge and tooling layer that keeps the project understandable. The wiki overview page and vault overview note are the human/LLM-facing knowledge bases capturing decisions and gotchas, and graphify-config.mjs is the shared loader behind the diagram tooling that produced the very graph this tour was built from. This is the meta-layer: how contributors (and agents) keep a mental model of a system this large in sync.

tour.title: How the Code Stays Correct
tour.description: Finish with the discipline that keeps everything above trustworthy. The test suite is deliberately framework-free — Node's built-in node:test for TypeScript and #[cfg(test)] for Rust, zero dependencies, matching the hand-rolled style of server.ts and tui.ts. Coverage targets the pure logic core rather than the React tree: tool-repair.test.ts pins the deterministic repair layer that rescues weak local models, and csv-import.test.ts covers the ingestion pipeline end to end (delimiter sniffing, Exasol identifier folding, type inference, SQL literal escaping) — the path where a bug means data corruption or injection. Run it all with `pnpm test`. The KISS hard rules in CLAUDE.md explain the boundaries these tests enforce: no file reaching 5,000 lines, no unreachable code, nothing too big to test.
